hints: Focus on the word only. Ask yourself for each target, do human body cells also use this process or structure?
Compare transcription, translation, DNA replication and cell wall building. Which one of these four targets is completely absent from human cells?
walkthrough:
**Understand what only means**

Great question to slow down for. We need a process that happens in bacteria but does NOT happen in our own human cells. If human cells also do it, the antibiotic could harm us too.

**Check 1, 2 and 3**

Human cells also make RNA using RNA polymerase, so 1 is shared. Human cells also make DNA and make proteins using ribosomes, so 2 and 3 are shared too. Even though our cytoplasmic ribosomes are 80S, our mitochondria have 70S-like ribosomes that can be affected.

**Check 4 and conclude**

Peptidoglycan is the special polymer in bacterial cell walls. Human cells have no cell wall and make no peptidoglycan at all. So inhibiting peptidoglycan synthesis hits bacteria only, which means 4 only is correct.

options.A: Incorrect, because 1, 2 and 3 target processes that human cells also carry out, so they are not bacteria-only.
options.B: Incorrect, because RNA polymerase, ribosomes and DNA synthesis are all found in human cells, including mitochondria.
options.C: Incorrect, because although 4 is bacteria-only, 2 is not, since mitochondrial ribosomes are 70S-like and can be inhibited.
options.D: Correct, because only peptidoglycan synthesis is unique to bacteria. Humans have no peptidoglycan, so ampicillin affects bacterial cells only.
